summary: Monads in natural-language semantics. The three monad laws for the powerset, reader and continuation monads, stated pointwise; Shan's lifted application in each; Giorgolo and Asudeh's opacity readings on a small model; and two scope readings that differ on a model.

sources.citation: Shan, C. (2001). Monads for natural language semantics. Proc. ESSLLI 2001 Student Session, pp. 285-298 (arXiv:cs/0205026).
sources.available: read in full; section 3 is not formalized

sources.citation: Giorgolo, G. & Asudeh, A. (2014). Monads as a solution for generalized opacity. Proc. EACL 2014 Workshop TTNLS, pp. 19-27.

theorems.name: set_monad_laws
theorems.source_claim: T1. Left identity, right identity and associativity [Shan (24.3a-c), fn. 1 p. 286] for the powerset monad (24.4), as equivalences of membership.

theorems.name: reader_monad_laws
theorems.source_claim: T2. The three laws (24.3a-c) for the reader monad (24.16), as equalities at every index w.

theorems.name: cont_monad_laws
theorems.source_claim: T3. The three laws (24.3a-c) for the continuation monad (24.19), as equalities at every continuation c.

theorems.name: lifted_application
theorems.source_claim: T4. Lifted application in the three monads: (24.9), (24.17), (24.21).

theorems.name: secondary_rule
theorems.source_claim: T5. The secondary rule in the three monads: A'_M f x = A_M f (unit x).

theorems.name: AM_set
theorems.source_claim: T4a. In the powerset monad A_M f x = { a b | a in f, b in x }. [Shan (24.9), p. 288]: pointwise function application over alternatives.

theorems.name: AM_reader
theorems.source_claim: T4b. In the reader monad A_M f x = fun w => f w (x w). [Shan (24.17), p. 289]

theorems.name: AM_cont
theorems.source_claim: T4c. In the continuation monad A_M f x = fun c => f (fun g => x (fun y => c (g y))). [Shan (24.21), p. 290]

theorems.name: reader_commutative
theorems.source_claim: T6a. The reader monad is commutative: the order in which two computations are bound does not matter. G&A fn. 6 p. 23 use this to identify readings that differ only in that order.

theorems.name: transparent_substitution
theorems.source_claim: T6b. Transparency of bind (ours; it is what makes G&A's reading (32) contradictory): if a and b have the same value at index i, then binding either into the same continuation gives the same result at i.

theorems.name: m1_bind_k1
theorems.source_claim: m1 * k1 has exactly the four members Shan lists on p. 287, for any two relations like and hate.

theorems.name: john_smokes
theorems.source_claim: [[John smokes]] evaluates to smoke(John). [Shan (24.20) and p. 291]

theorems.name: john_smokes_true
theorems.source_claim: stated in the file; see its header

theorems.name: everyone_smokes
theorems.source_claim: [[everyone smokes]] evaluates to "for all x, smoke x". [Shan p. 291]

theorems.name: everyone_smokes_false
theorems.source_claim: stated in the file; see its header

theorems.name: everyone_not_pure
theorems.source_claim: everyone is not unit of any individual: it uses its continuation non-trivially. [Shan p. 291, remark after (24.22)]

theorems.name: fun_first_reading
theorems.source_claim: With Shan's A_M (function first) the object quantifier takes widest scope.

theorems.name: arg_first_reading
theorems.source_claim: With the argument evaluated first (AMr, ours) the subject takes widest scope.

theorems.name: scope_readings_differ
theorems.source_claim: S1a. Separating example: on the model the two scope readings differ.

theorems.name: cont_not_commutative
theorems.source_claim: S1b. Separating example: the continuation monad is NOT commutative (contrast T6a for the reader monad).

theorems.name: opacity_readings
theorems.source_claim: T8. The three readings together: (33), (34) and (30) of G&A.

theorems.name: reading31_truth_conditions
theorems.source_claim: T8a. Reading (31) has the truth conditions (33): Mary Jane loves pp and does not love the entity she calls Spider-Man. [G&A (33), p. 24]

theorems.name: reading32_contradictory
theorems.source_claim: T8b. Reading (32), evaluated at the speaker's index, has the unsatisfiable truth conditions (34), whatever the love relation. [G&A (34), p. 24]

theorems.name: reading29_contradictory
theorems.source_claim: T8c. Reading (29) is false at every index, whatever the punch relation: sentence (2) has only a contradictory reading. [G&A (30), p. 24]

theorems.name: reading31_true
theorems.source_claim: Computed results: (31) is true and (32) is false on the model.

theorems.name: reading32_false
theorems.source_claim: stated in the file; see its header

theorems.name: coreferring_at_sigma
theorems.source_claim: The two names co-refer for the speaker.

theorems.name: substitution_holds_outside
theorems.source_claim: Substitution holds OUTSIDE the scope of love: bound from outside (as in (32)), Spider-Man can be replaced by Peter Parker. Instance of T6b.

theorems.name: substitution_fails_under_love
theorems.source_claim: S2. Separating example: substitution FAILS inside the argument of love. Co-reference at the speaker's index does not license replacing one term by the other under an arbitrary function on monadic values.

evidence: DRAFT for the author's review; not an accepted source-level verdict.
The laws are stated pointwise, so no extensionality axiom is used.
Shan's monad morphisms and translations, the state and error monads, and Giorgolo and Asudeh's sequent calculus are not formalized.
Nothing is taken from Charlow's dissertation, which was not available.

determination_rationale: DRAFT for the author. The monads transpose directly; the opacity fragment is a small model.

artifact_classes.description: pointwise equality in place of equality of functions
